Kiln & Quire

Two printers in a former kiln shed below Gojō-zaka. We set wood and lead type by hand, run it through a 1960s Vandercook, then overprint it on the riso in inks that glow. Editions stay small — rarely more than forty — and on weekends we hand you the keys.

The Weekend Press

Two days, three inks, one edition of thirty — designed, set and printed by you. No experience needed. Ink under the nails guaranteed.

Dates
10–11 Oct · 24–25 Oct · 7–8 Nov · 21–22 Nov
Seats
6 per weekend
Fee

Taught in
English / 日本語
  1. Sat 10:00–16:00 · Pass 1 · Letterpress

    Set it in wood.

    Choose a face from the type cabinet, set your line by hand, lock it up and pull it on the Vandercook in blue. Letterpress bites into the sheet — you can read your words with a thumb.

  2. Sun 10:00–12:30 · Pass 2 · Riso yellow

    Split the colours.

    Draw every colour as its own black-and-white sheet. The riso burns a stencil master from each and lays down one ink at a time, never quite in register. That wobble is the look.

  3. Sun 13:30–16:00 · Pass 3 · Fluorescent pink

    Overprint.

    Riso ink is translucent. Pink over yellow prints a red nobody mixed; pink over blue, a violet; blue over yellow, a green. Three inks, seven colours, if you plan the overlaps.

  4. Sun 16:00 · Edition

    Number thirty.

    Every sheet takes a number from our old numbering machine. You carry the edition home; one print stays in the studio plan chest with your name on it.
